newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk coalition party sacks MP, cutting govt margin.
newsitem.headline: Turk coalition party sacks MP, cutting govt margin.

text.p: The conservative wing of Turkey's Islamist-led coalition on Monday expelled dissident deputy and former minister Yalim Erez, reducing the government's paper margin in parliament to just one seat, party officials said.
"The decision was taken to expel Mr Erez and he was informed of that decision," True Path Party (DYP) official Abdullah Uras told reporters after a party meeting.

His resignation left the coalition with just 274 seats in the 550-member assembly. The government is now two short of an absolute majority but effectively it would still have a margin of two seats in key votes.

Erez resigned his post as Trade and Industry Minister last month in a row over the reluctance of the Islamist wing of the coalition to act on military-led demands for a crackdown on Islamist activism. He had held talks with the opposition to try to form a secularist alliance to oust the Islamists.
On Sunday, Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan told a news conference his government was seeking early elections to defuse the row.
Under Turkish law, parliament must set the date for elections and approve the coalition's decision to make deputy leader Tansu Ciller the caretaker prime minister.
